claims: Artemis II is a ~10-day crewed mission.
Artemis II launches in April 2026.
Artemis II uses a figure-eight, free-return trajectory.
The Orion spacecraft will orbit Earth twice.
The Orion spacecraft will fly around the Moon's far side.
The Orion spacecraft will reach ~685,000+ miles total.
The Orion spacecraft will use lunar gravity to naturally return to Earth.
Artemis II launches from Kennedy Space Center.
The SLS rocket will place Orion into an initial high-Earth orbit.
The crew will perform two orbits of Earth.
The crew will perform systems checkouts.
The crew will perform a simulated docking with the spent upper stage.
Orion will ignite its service module engine to leave Earth orbit.
Orion will loop around the far side of the Moon.
The spacecraft passes approx. 10,300 km past the Moon.
Artemis II will set a new record for human distance from Earth.
The trajectory leverages the Moon's gravity to swing the spacecraft back toward Earth.
The trajectory does not require complex, fuel-heavy maneuvers.
Orion will re-enter Earth's atmosphere at 10.99 km/s.
Orion will land in the Pacific Ocean.
Artemis II has a crew of four astronauts.
Artemis II is designed to test critical systems for future lunar landings
